### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.test

### Description

I would be interested in doing the work for this but before going that route I wanted to know if it is something you would be interested (or if there is a way to do it already that I have missed).

I propose adding the necessary hooks within the main and child processes to allow waiting on a debugger connection, in this case One-Small-Step-For-Vimkind. I am unsure if it can be generic enough to support various debuggers, as OSV is the one I am looking to integrate.

Having a means to toggle the debugger flow using a function that can be called through a keymap would make it seamless with the development process, versus what I currently do which is some very long sleeps to ensure I have time to attach nvim-dap, which I have to remember to remove when I am done.

A change on the OSV-side will also be needed to notify a listener that a connection has been made, but that should be pretty trivial and the maintainer has shown interest in the past (https://github.com/jbyuki/one-small-step-for-vimkind/issues/48) so I would coordinate on that side as well.

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the suggestion!

I don't really have much experience with debuggers as I mostly work with interpreted languages. The workflow for debugging tests written with 'mini.test' is mostly to modify tested module/plugin to write to global `_G.log` table and the examining it in proper places with `eq(child.lua_get('_G.log'))`.

Could you please describe how would the potential code on the user side look (i.e. how test writer would use it) and the whole workflow? To be upfront, as I have high doubts that this is possible to implement concisely, it is not very likely to become part of the 'mini.test'. But I'd like to be more informed before making this decision.

Of course!

They would need two instances of NeoVim opened, one to run the test (I will call it the debuggee) and one to go debug the code and step through the code (the debugger). The osv plugin would be required in the `deps` folder to be accessible and be accessible to the child processes, and `nvim-dap` in the debugger instance.

In the debugger, one would set a breakpoint on a line of code (eg the first line of the main init.lua's config() function).

In the debuggee, they would press a keybind to activate the mini debug mode.
They would then execute a test, which before running the test code (possibly before the test's pre-test hook) would launch the OSV server which will listen on a given port for a debugger connection.
The code would then actively wait for an event from OSV confirming a debugger connected.
Today I achieve this by calling `child.lua([[require("osv").launch({ port = 8086 })]])` in the pre_case hook, and doing a `vim.loop.sleep(10000)` in each test I want to debug.

They would then go to the debugger instance, and using a keybind connect to the above port.

Back in the debuggee, now that a connection has been made, the code would run normally up until the breakpoint where the code would stop executing.

In the debugger, one can then evaluate variables, execute the code step by step to see which lines get executed, etc.
Then once they are done debugging, they would use a keybind to resume execution flow, which would release the debuggee to finish running.

If ever you would rather not integrate this feature directly, I should be able to achieve similar results with a global pre-test hook. Though once one starts using debuggers it is hard to stop using them as they are awesome, so I figured lowering the bar of entry would be good. :)

Let me know if you want more details!

Thanks for such a detailed clarification! This all sounds useful and relatively similar to what I know about using debuggers.

> Today I achieve this by calling `child.lua([[require("osv").launch({ port = 8086 })]])` in the pre_case hook, and doing a `vim.loop.sleep(10000)` in each test I want to debug.

I guess my question is what changes do you suggest to be done directly with 'mini.test'?

Having to add a `child.lua('require("osv").launch({ port = 8086 })')` line to initiate debugger doesn't sound problematic to me (as it can be wrapped into custom helper like `child.start_osv()`).

If having to use `vim.loop.sleep(10000)` is the problem here, then I *think* using `vim.wait` inside child process after launching OSV should be doable. It will wait until it registers that the launch has completed, as long as there is a way to check that. So something like this:

```lua
child.lua([[
  require("osv").launch({ port = 8086 })
  local is_osv_launched = function() ... end
  vim.wait(10000, is_osv_launched, 1)
]])
```

A slightly less performant but separate approach is to define in the parent instance `wait_for_osv` like this (although some initial tests show this is might interfere with 'mini.test' reporters):

```lua
local is_osv_launched = function() return child.lua_get('...') end
local wait_for_osv = function() vim.wait(10000, is_osv_launched, 10) end
```

Since every test is a potential candidate to be debugged at one time or another, having to repeat the pattern on every single test creates a lot of noise in the test definitions and takes away from the underlying test (imo).
So I was looking for a centralized approach with a built-in command to toggle on or off the debugging feature, in your example it would not launch osv nor wait until it is launched/connected to.
So in essence it would be something like:
```lua
MiniTest.debugger = function()
  --hook to launch the server
  require("osv").launch({ port = 8086 })
end,
function() 
  --hook to check if a connection is made
  -- content of is_osv_launched
  end
end
```
And internally these two would be wrapped by a conditional to only be called when the debugger functionality is active.
~~Now you mention custom child helpers and I feel like I missed that, it sounds promising, how would I add one?~~ Nevermind I read up on field injection in Lua.
Also, I did not know you could use wait with a function, that's a good one to add to my toolbelt!

> ... in your example it would not launch osv nor wait until it is launched/connected to.

I don't understand this. It essentially does "... calling `child.lua([[require("osv").launch({ port = 8086 })]])` in the pre_case hook, and doing a `vim.loop.sleep(10000)` in each test I want to debug." but with "smart" waiting on child side. Could you elaborate, please?

> So in essence it would be something like:
> 
> MiniTest.debugger = function()
>   --hook to launch the server
>   require("osv").launch({ port = 8086 })
> end,
> function() 
>   --hook to check if a connection is made
>   -- content of is_osv_launched
>   end
> end

In the initial clarification `require("osv").launch({ port = 8086 })` is executed inside child process, while this code assumes execution in parent/testing process. I would assume that this wrapper would be a method of `new_child_neovim()` output. What do I miss here?

> ~Now you mention custom child helpers and I feel like I missed that, it sounds promising, how would I add one?~ Nevermind I read up on field injection in Lua.

Yes, essentially create a wrapper around `MiniTest.new_child_neovim()` and add new methods/fields to the child process. This is the route ['mini.nvim' tests themselves take](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/fe8a669078a5066220262f173bf901f322e39c05/tests/helpers.lua#L60-L185).

The alternative is to create wrappers like `local get_child_size = function(child) return { child.o.lines, child.o.columns } end`. But I find `child.get_size()` easier to understand (as it has the same structure as other child methods) than `get_child_size(child)`.

So in my mind it would be something like this in the test file:

```lua
local child = MiniTest.new_child_neovim()

child.debug = function()
  child.lua([[
    require("osv").launch({ port = 8086 })
    local is_osv_launched = function()
      -- An actual logic that tests whether OSV finished launching
    end
    vim.wait(10000, is_osv_launched, 1)
  ]])
end
```

Then manually add `child.debug()` inside problematic test and run it with [`run_at_location()`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/fe8a669078a5066220262f173bf901f322e39c05/doc/mini-test.txt#L394). Does this make sense or am I missing something (I have feeling that I do)?
I will put a prototype together as it will be much easier to discuss over actual code :)

> I will put a prototype together as it will be much easier to discuss over actual code :)

It would be indeed. I just was hesitant of asking this because it is still a "probably a bit too much for 'mini.test'" situation and a very likely "this is out of scope" issue resolution. One major indicator here (besides the usual "adds complexity and lines") is that it requires several plugins outside of 'mini.nvim' ('nvim-dap' and OSV at least). As there is long way for the debugger/DAP integration into 'mini.nvim', if there will ever be one (it is tracked in #638).

But I am open to adding a section to 'TESTING.md' if custom helper code is concise enough, though.
No worries if anything it exposes me to more Lua code which I do not have much experience with.

So I failed to write something that works in a short time (I have not gotten the hang of how comm works with the child processes for configs, etc).
However i think the 'changes' explain how I envision the change could be, keeping it generic and not specific to OSV.
You can see the commit here (very rough, not something I would create a PR for): https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/commit/22ddc5a9b556d025efd755ffdb41f6cd367fe96c

Here is a snippet of code with how it could be used, though if possible I think some of it should be part of the config file instead (see in-line comments). I have put the related code in between --> and --<, the rest is just a typical test, but I left it there for context.

```lua
local reference_screenshot = MiniTest.expect.reference_screenshot
local child_helper = require("tests.child_helper")
local child = child_helper.new_child_neovim()
local env = require("tests.env")

--> Start of related code
-- Ok so this does not actually execute, but it should convey the idea pretty well
-- I think putting this in the config would make more sense, see comment in declaration
MiniTest.debug_pre_case_hook = function()
  child.lua([[
    require("osv").launch({ port = 8086 })

    local wait_for_osv = function()
      -- then osv function/callback does not exist yet so doing a sleep for the prototype
      vim.loop.sleep(10000)
      return true
    end

    vim.wait(10000, wait_for_osv, 1)
  ]])
end

-- See comment in declaration on this
MiniTest.execute_debug_hooks = true
--< end of related code

local T = MiniTest.new_set({
  hooks = {
    pre_once = function()
      if vim.fn.filereadable("./tests/logs/test_suggestion.log") == 1 then
        vim.fn.delete("./tests/logs/test_suggestion.log")
      end
    end,
    pre_case = function()
      child.restart({ "-u", "tests/scripts/minimal_init.lua" })
      child.bo.readonly = false
      child.lua("M = require('copilot')")
      child.lua("cmd = require('copilot.command')")
      child.fn.setenv("GITHUB_COPILOT_TOKEN", env.COPILOT_TOKEN)
    end,
    post_once = child.stop,
  },
})

T["suggestion()"] = MiniTest.new_set()

T["suggestion()"]["suggestion works"] = function()
  child.o.lines, child.o.columns = 10, 15
  child.lua([[
    M.setup({ })
  ]])

  child.wait_for_copilot_init()
  child.type_keys("i123", "<Esc>", "o456", "<Esc>", "o7")
  vim.loop.sleep(3000)
  child.lua("vim.wait(0)")

  reference_screenshot(child.get_screenshot())
end
```

Thanks for the follow up.

If [adding dedicated conditional hooks](https://github.com/AntoineGS/mini.nvim/commit/22ddc5a9b556d025efd755ffdb41f6cd367fe96c) (one for before `pre_case` and one for after `post_case`) is all takes, then it is indeed something better handled in the project's setup (if it wants to support using debuggers). Adding the same functionality as calls in the first line of global (for global `T`) `pre_case` hooks and last line of global `post_case` hook should be equivalent to what is shown in the commit.

So it would be something like this:

```lua
-- ...

local debug_pre_case_hook = function()
  if not _G.execute_minitest_debug_hooks then return end
  -- ...
end

local T = MiniTest.new_set({
  hooks = {
    pre_once = function()
      -- ...
    end,
    pre_case = function()
      debug_pre_case_hook()
      -- ...
    end,
    post_once = child.stop,
  },
})
```

Then have a mapping that toggles `_G.execute_minitest_debug_hooks` (set in global namespace for user to actually "own" it).

---

All in all, I do think that this would be either too complex and dependent on other plugins to add to 'mini.test' *or* indeed truly more comfortable to be added as custom project helper. So I am going to close this as "probably not planned; at least not until there is something debugging related in 'mini.nvim' directly".

If you figure out an approach that works for you, please leave a comment. It might be a good candidate to include in 'TESTING.md' if it is concise enough. And if you have specific questions about how something is better done here, feel free to ask (with maybe more "explain me like I'm five" context and/or code).
I appreciate the time you took to discuss this 🙂

In the event that someone else wants to replicate this, here is how I achieved the behavior with OSV.
Points of interest are:
- `child_helper.run_pre_case()`
- `child_helper.configure_copilot()`
- Code related to `_G.attach_debugger`

My test file, `test_sometest.lua`:
```lua
local reference_screenshot = MiniTest.expect.reference_screenshot
local child_helper = require("tests.child_helper")
local child = child_helper.new_child_neovim("test_suggestion")

local T = MiniTest.new_set({
  hooks = {
    pre_once = function() end,
    pre_case = function()
      child.run_pre_case()
      child.bo.readonly = false
      child.lua("M = require('copilot')")
    end,
    post_once = child.stop,
  },
})

T["suggestion()"] = MiniTest.new_set()

T["suggestion()"]["suggestion works"] = function()
  child.o.lines, child.o.columns = 10, 15
  child.config.suggestion = child.config.suggestion .. "auto_trigger = true,"
  child.configure_copilot()
  child.type_keys("i123", "<Esc>", "o456", "<Esc>", "o7")
  child.wait_for_suggestion()

  reference_screenshot(child.get_screenshot())
end
```

The `child_helper.lua` file:
```lua
local env = require("tests.env")
local M = {}

if not _G.attach_debugger then
  _G.attach_debugger = false
end

---@param test_name string
function M.new_child_neovim(test_name)
  ---@class MiniTest.child
  local child = MiniTest.new_child_neovim()
  local logfile = string.format("./tests/logs/%s.log", test_name)
  child.config = nil

  if vim.fn.filereadable(logfile) == 1 then
    vim.fn.delete(logfile)
  end

  function child.reset_config()
    child.config = {
      panel = "",
      suggestion = [[
        suggestion_notification = function(virt_text, _)
          if (#virt_text > 0) and (#virt_text[1] > 0) and (virt_text[1][1] == "89") then
            M.suggested = true
          end
        end,
      ]],
      logger = string.format(
        [[
        file_log_level = vim.log.levels.TRACE,
        file = "%s",
      ]],
        logfile
      ),
      server = "",
      root_dir = "",
      should_attach = "",
      filetypes = [[
        ["*"] = true,
      ]],
      auth_provider_url = "",
      workspace_folders = "",
      server_opts_overrides = "",
      copilot_model = "",
      copilot_node_command = "",
    }
  end

  function child.setup_and_wait_for_debugger()
    if not _G.attach_debugger then
      return
    end

    child.lua([[
      require("osv").launch({ port = 8086, blocking = true })
    ]])
  end

  function child.run_pre_case()
    child.reset_config()
    child.restart({ "-u", "tests/scripts/minimal_init.lua" })
    if env.COPILOT_TOKEN and env.COPILOT_TOKEN ~= "" then
      child.fn.setenv("GITHUB_COPILOT_TOKEN", env.COPILOT_TOKEN)
    end
    child.setup_and_wait_for_debugger()
  end

  function child.configure_copilot()
    local script = ""
    for k, v in pairs(child.config) do
      if v ~= "" and v ~= nil then
        if type(v) == "string" then
          script = string.format(
            [[%s%s = {
          %s
          },
          ]],
            script,
            k,
            v
          )
        end
      end
    end

    script = string.format(
      [[
        M.suggested = false
        M.setup({ %s })
      ]],
      script
    )

    child.lua(script)

    child.lua([[
      local copilot_is_initialized = function()
        local client = require("copilot.client")
        return client.initialized
      end

      vim.wait(30000, copilot_is_initialized, 10)
    ]])
  end

  function child.wait_for_suggestion()
    child.lua([[
      vim.wait(30000, function()
        return M.suggested
      end, 10)
    ]])
  end

  return child
end

return M
```

The key definition to toggle on and off the debugger hook:
```lua
    { "<leader>dd", function ()
      _G.attach_debugger = not _G.attach_debugger
      print("Debugger: " .. (_G.attach_debugger and "ON" or "OFF"))
    end, desc = "Toggle Attach Debugger"},
```

> In the event that someone else wants to replicate this, here is how I achieved the behavior with OSV.

Thanks for sharing!

As it has *too* much non-debugger related code, here are the relevant parts:

- Make sure that child process contains OSV plugin in its 'runtimepath'.
- Put this code in the global `pre_case`
    ```lua
    if not _G.attach_debugger then return end
    child.lua('require("osv").launch({ port = 8086, blocking = true })')
    ```
- To toggle whether a debugger should be attached, toggle the `_G.attach_debugger` global variable like `_G.attach_debugger = not _G.attach_debugger`.
